Earlier reports claimed that Apple was preparing to launch a 20th anniversary edition iPhone next year, featuring an all-glass design. However, analysts at investment bank Jefferies believe the device is no longer moving forward.

Wall Street analysts say the bold redesign plans for the 20th anniversary iPhone have been cancelled.

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies today downgraded Apple's stock rating to "Underperform", with analyst Edison Lee noting that the possible cancellation of the 20th anniversary iPhone redesign is one of the main reasons behind the downgrade.

The key to this downgrade lies in the reported cancellation of Apple's all-glass iPhone project. Although rumours about the project being under development surfaced as early as 2025, with some believing it could launch in 2027, Apple has never responded to these speculations. However, the company quietly filed a patent for an "all-glass enclosure" as early as 2019. Jefferies had previously considered the launch of an all-glass iPhone to be reasonable and credible, but Lee believes development work has stalled. The analyst noted that supply chain checks indicate the project was terminated due to poor yield rates. Lee believes that with memory costs soaring, this decision deals a "major blow" to driving high-end iPhone sales. Had the device launched as scheduled in September 2027 to celebrate iPhone's 20th anniversary, he projected the blended retail price would reach US$2,060, higher than the average selling price of any previous model. Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe Apple originally planned to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models to further increase average selling prices and margins." He believes that with memory prices rising, this move would have been a crucial defensive strategy.

Lee also pointed out that Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are additional reasons behind the stock downgrade.

From Lee's report, it is not entirely clear whether the analyst believes the entire redesign plan has been shelved, or only certain design elements have been abandoned.

The most upvoted comment was posted by Currentinterest.

These analysts have been wrong too many times about Apple's future plans. Even the term "all-glass" may never have accurately reflected Apple's true intentions. The 20th anniversary phone will be unique and innovative, and will sell well no matter what the final design turns out to be.

For example, there have long been speculations that Apple will not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. Therefore, an "all-glass" screen will not be possible. However, the rumoured four-curved-edge design could still potentially launch.

In any case, if the iPhone 20th anniversary design has indeed been cancelled, credible media outlets should confirm it soon.

What do you all think about this report regarding the iPhone 20th anniversary design? Let us know in the comments.
